why: Story 45.5, FR-178. The pinning between keeper_core::size::format_file_size and its TypeScript mirror src/lib/file-size.ts. Both are loaded from THIS file by their own test suites, so a change to either implementation fails on the same commit that introduces it. A mirror that is only documented as a mirror drifts; a mirror that shares a vector table cannot drift silently. Bytes are strings because a JSON number cannot hold u64::MAX exactly and this table has to be able to say what the largest possible file renders as.
baseWhy: Decimal. macOS Finder has reported decimal sizes since 10.6 and keeper is macOS-first: the number keeper puts beside a file must be the number the operating system puts beside the same file, or the user concludes one of them is lying.

vectors.label: 0 bytes
vectors.why: an empty file exists and is worth saying so about; it is a DIRECTORY that must render nothing at all

vectors.label: 1 byte
vectors.why: the singular

vectors.label: 2 bytes
vectors.why: the plural resumes immediately above the singular

vectors.label: 999 bytes
vectors.why: one below the base: still exact, still a word

vectors.label: 1.0 kB
vectors.why: the base itself; lowercase SI k, never KB and never KiB

vectors.label: 1.0 kB
vectors.why: one below the BINARY boundary, which is not a boundary here

vectors.label: 1.0 kB
vectors.why: 1024 bytes is 1.024 kB, not 1 KiB. This vector is the whole decimal decision

vectors.label: 1.5 kB
vectors.why: one decimal place below ten

vectors.label: 1.9 kB
vectors.why: truncation, not rounding: 1.999 is 1.9 and never 2.0

vectors.label: 9.9 kB
vectors.why: the last value that still gets a decimal place

vectors.label: 10 kB
vectors.why: at ten the decimal place is dropped

vectors.label: 999 kB
vectors.why: one below the next unit; a rounding implementation prints the impossible 1000.0 kB here

vectors.label: 1.0 MB
vectors.why: the MB step

vectors.label: 1.0 MB
vectors.why: one mebibyte. Both chat surfaces printed this as 1.0 MB by dividing by 1024, which was the right string for the wrong reason and the wrong string for 1500000

vectors.label: 1.5 MB
vectors.why: the value that exposes a binary divisor: a 1024-based formatter calls this 1.4 MB

vectors.label: 999 MB
vectors.why: one below the GB step

vectors.label: 1.0 GB
vectors.why: the GB step

vectors.label: 2.5 GB
vectors.why: a file big enough to need GB

vectors.label: 5.0 GB
vectors.why: a recording-sized file

vectors.label: 12 GB
vectors.why: at and above ten, no decimal, in a unit above kB

vectors.label: 999 GB
vectors.why: one below the TB step

vectors.label: 1.0 TB
vectors.why: the TB step

vectors.label: 1.0 PB
vectors.why: the PB step

vectors.label: 1.0 EB
vectors.why: the EB step; the top rung of the ladder

vectors.label: 18 EB
vectors.why: u64::MAX. An implementation that multiplies before dividing overflows here, and a ladder that stops at PB prints 18446 PB. In JavaScript this exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, which is why the mirror takes a bigint and this column is a string
